sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Oro Valley, AZ?
sections.html:
A sale in Oro Valley runs through Pima County, not Maricopa County, and the town has its own short-term rental license, so the paperwork differs from the Phoenix area. The town sits in the foothills north of Tucson, and Census figures show an older population and a high median household income.

This page walks through the town's layout and history, the schools that serve it, the local rules a seller should know, the Pima County recording steps and the property tax dates.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Oro Valley homes and owners?
sections.html:
Oro Valley is a small town of 48,085 people by the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $475,700 for 2020 to 2024. The figures below are for the town.

More than a third of residents are 65 or older, and households average 2.20 people. Wikipedia adds that many residents keep second or winter homes in town, so a seller may be dealing with an owner who lives elsewhere part of the year.

The population grew from 41,011 in 2010 to 47,070 in 2020, a gain of about 15 percent, and the estimate since then shows slower growth of 2.2 percent.

sections.h2: How did Oro Valley become a town?
sections.html:
Oro Valley incorporated in 1974 with only 2.4 square miles and about 1,200 residents, after a fight with Tucson and Pima County over its future. Tucson's mayor had spoken of bringing the area into the city, and a 1968 petition to incorporate was refused by the Pima County Board of Supervisors before the Arizona Supreme Court ruled in favor of incorporation. The founders had called the place Palo Verde before choosing Oro Valley.

The settlement history is older. The Hohokam lived at Honey Bee Village in the Tortolita foothills from about AD 450, and George Pusch ran a cattle ranch with a steam pump from 1874 at what is now Steam Pump Ranch, which joined the National Register of Historic Places in September 2009. The first suburban development, Campo Bello, began in 1948, and Suffolk Hills went up between 1960 and 1962. Most early homes were built by individual owners on large lots.

sections.h2: Where is Oro Valley, and what does the land look like?
sections.html:
Oro Valley is about 6 miles north of Tucson in Pima County, at an elevation of roughly 2,620 feet. The Cañada del Oro wash runs through the middle of town, the Santa Catalina Mountains and Pusch Ridge rise on the east, and the Tortolita Mountains sit to the north. Catalina State Park and the Coronado National Forest form the eastern edge.

The town's permit guidance says a lot may carry conservation easements, utility easements or floodplain areas that limit where structures can go, so check the survey and recorded easements before you promise a buyer a pool or an addition.

Parks that buyers ask about include Naranja Park (213 acres), Cañada del Oro Riverfront Park and James D. Kriegh Park.

Amphitheater Public Schools runs the public schools in Oro Valley. Its high schools here are Canyon del Oro High School, which opened in 1962, and Ironwood Ridge High School, which opened in 2001. The district also operates elementary schools, two K-8 schools and a middle school in the town.

Charter and private options include BASIS Schools Oro Valley (K-12), Leman Academy of Excellence (K-8), Casas Christian School, Pusch Ridge Christian Academy and Immaculate Heart Preparatory School. Ask the district to confirm the school assigned to a specific address before you quote it to a buyer.

sections.h2: Can an Oro Valley house be a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Yes. Short-term rentals are allowed by right in all residential districts in Oro Valley, but a homeowners association can restrict them and the town requires a license. Town Ordinance (O)23-01 took effect February 3, 2023, and enforcement began May 6, 2023.

The town's rules and its FAQ cover these points:

  • The license fee is $80, the same as a Town business license.
  • The owner needs a state Transaction Privilege Tax license that lists Oro Valley.
  • The rental must be registered with the Pima County Assessor under A.R.S. 33-1902.
  • Applicants show liability insurance of at least $500,000, or a booking platform that supplies equal coverage.
  • Neighbors receive a notification, and the license number appears on rental promotions.

The town does not inspect proactively and acts on complaints. If you are selling a house that has been rented this way, tell the buyer what license and HOA terms apply.

sections.h2: How do you check permits on an Oro Valley house before selling?
sections.html:
Call the town's Community and Economic Development Department at 520-229-4800 or email Permits@orovalleyaz.gov. The town's permit guide lists pools and spas, pool heaters and grading among the work that can need a permit, and it tells owners to confirm with the Planning Division that a project meets the zoning standards even when no permit is required.

Gather your permit history before you list:

  • Any addition, garage or remodel.
  • A pool, spa or pool heater.
  • Walls, sheds and grading work.

If a permit is missing, raise it with the town before an offer comes in, not during escrow.

sections.h2: How is an Oro Valley deed recorded in Pima County?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Pima County Recorder along with an affidavit of property value, and the recorder lists the affidavit form as available from the Arizona Department of Revenue. Recording any document costs a flat $30.00 under A.R.S. 11-475, according to the Recorder's fee schedule last revised April 15, 2022.

Pima County has two recording offices, at 240 N Stone Avenue downtown and at 6920 E Broadway Blvd, Suite D. Since September 8, 2026, anyone presenting a document in person must show valid photo identification under A.R.S. 11-472, and documents received after 4 p.m. Tucson time are processed the next business day. Your title company usually handles the filing for you.

sections.h2: When are Oro Valley property taxes due?
sections.html:
Arizona property tax is split into two halves, due October 1 and March 1. Under A.R.S. 42-18052, the first half is delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after 5:00 p.m. on May 1, and bills of $100 or less are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

Because November 1 has passed, ask the Pima County Treasurer whether the first half on your parcel is paid before you close. Your title company will show how the current year's tax is divided between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Do you need a license to rent a house short term in Oro Valley?
faqs.a: Yes. Oro Valley requires a short-term rental license, which costs $80, and the owner must also hold a state Transaction Privilege Tax license and register the rental with the Pima County Assessor. A homeowners association can add its own limits.

faqs.q: Which county records a deed for an Oro Valley house?
faqs.a: Pima County. The Pima County Recorder records the deed and charges a flat $30.00 per document, and the sale needs an affidavit of property value from the Arizona Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Do I need photo ID to record a document in Pima County?
faqs.a: Yes, in person. Since September 8, 2026, the Pima County Recorder requires valid photo identification from anyone presenting a document for recording at its counter.

faqs.q: Who serves the public schools in Oro Valley?
faqs.a: Amphitheater Public Schools. Its high schools in the town are Canyon del Oro and Ironwood Ridge. Confirm the assigned school for a specific address with the district.

faqs.q: When is the Arizona property tax first-half deadline?
faqs.a: The first half is due October 1 and goes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1. The second half is due March 1 and goes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 1.
